evidence: TaskController.register binds Express routes to handlers. This is transport wiring.
createTask reads the request body and builds a CreateTaskInput, then calls this.service.createTask. This maps input and delegates to the service.
requiredText, optionalText and routeParam only check types and presence of raw HTTP input. They do not check business rules.
listTasks casts status to CreateTaskInput['status'] without checking it, so value validation stays with the service or domain.
errorHandler maps InvalidInputError to 400, TaskAlreadyDoneError to 409 and ResourceNotFoundError to 404. This is HTTP error translation, which belongs in transport.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file is an Express HTTP adapter, which is the job of an infrastructure (transport) layer. Everything it does fits that role. It registers routes, reads the request body, query and route parameters, checks the basic shape of the input (is this a string, is it present), builds the application's input DTOs, passes each call to TaskService, and turns the results into HTTP status codes and JSON responses. errorHandler only maps exception types to HTTP status codes (400, 409, 404, 500). The controller never checks business rules itself: valid status values, assignee membership and done-state changes are all left to the application and domain layers. It just casts status and hands it on. It also contains no persistence logic.
